question: Should I approve the $284K Staff SWE band exception?

intro.title: Meet Maya Chen
intro.text: HR Business Partner, People & Culture, Singapore. 2,412 employees, 18 pending PTO requests, one $284K offer decision — all before 15:00.

hero.title: The day, already triaged
hero.text: Her brief leads with what matters: the $284K Staff SWE band exception and an 18-deep PTO queue, cleared before Priya's 13:00 attrition deep-dive.

kpis.title: People metrics, live
kpis.text: Attrition at 11.4%, down 0.8 points. Offer acceptance up to 87.5%. Pulled straight from Workday and Greenhouse — no dashboard hunting.

chart.title: Twelve months, one story
chart.text: Engineering attrition fell from a 15.6% February peak to 11.9%. Stay interviews and the May comp-band refresh did that — the chart shows it.

ask.title: Drag data, ask hard questions
ask.text: Maya drags the offer card into chat and asks the day's toughest call: approve the $284K band exception, or hold the line?

delegate.title: Delegate the chasing
delegate.text: One click chases the $48,500 Deloitte engagement letter through DocuSign. Priya signed within 2 hours; only James's counter-signature remains.

autopilot.title: Autopilot clears the queue
autopilot.text: Flip the switch and low-risk approvals clear themselves — 13 conflict-free PTO requests and a Greenhouse access grant, gone. Only the offer needs Maya.

mcp.title: Every system, one console
mcp.text: Workday, Greenhouse, DocuSign — eight live connections under the hood. This is why the answers arrive with real numbers attached.

recap.title: Friday report, one click
recap.text: The week writes itself: 16.5 meeting hours, 6 Support reqs opened, HR-468 closed two days early. Ready to send before Friday lunch.

outro.title: Maya, at full speed
outro.text: Same Maya, same day — minus the chasing, the queues, and the tab-hopping. FoW handles the busywork; she makes the calls.
